title: Blueprint node closing the Frey package: Wiles_Frey and solution
intent: Close the Frey package: from a Frey package P derive False by composing four chapter theorems — Mazur_Frey (irreducibility), frey_isModular (modularity), level_lowering_to_two (a nonzero weight-2 cusp form on Gamma0 2) and S2_Gamma0_2_eq_zero (no such form exists) — with no proof of its own beyond the applications.

parent.name: solution
parent.note: The headline theorem of the file: a Frey package is impossible. The parent site also holds the auxiliary `Wiles_Frey` (lines 139-142), the in-file lemma that performs the contradiction, so the glue is the 9 lines of the two declarations together.

applicability.goal_shape: A target theorem `solution : False` (a contradiction) whose proof is nothing but applications of a few named chapter theorems imported from sibling files: a `let ⟨f, hf⟩ := level_lowering_to_two P (frey_isModular P) hirr` destructuring, then applying another lemma to the witness `f`, then applying a final lemma to close.
applicability.use_when: the project publishes a dependency graph (a blueprint or Prove2Me path) where each chapter result is a named theorem in its own file, and the closing node is a short composition of those names with no argument of its own in between.
applicability.avoid_when: the glue needs its own nontrivial proof — a real argument between the lemmas rather than a chain of applications; the lemmas are not already stated as named declarations; or the combination has to be discovered rather than read off the published graph.

consequences: The node creates four obligations, each discharged by a separate chapter theorem in its own file, and none by the glue itself; if any of the four were missing or mis-stated the closing node would fail to typecheck, so the correctness of the decomposition lives entirely in the exact types of the four chapter theorems. The glue relies on the last component of each name resolving to the imported theorem (via `p2m_open`), and on `let ⟨f, hf⟩ := ...` matching the existential that `level_lowering_to_two` produces; a change to that child's conclusion (e.g. a different congruence subgroup or weight) silently breaks the closing node.
